---
title: "Archimedes' Principle"
subtitle: "From Volume to Buoyant Force"
---

# Engineering Question

In the previous chapter we learned that pressure changes the volume of every gas carried by a diver. Yet volume alone cannot make a diver move.

How does a change in volume become an upward force?

This chapter derives Archimedes' Principle from the hydrostatic pressure field and interprets it as the transformation from **volume** to **force**.

# Learning Objectives

- Explain hydrostatic pressure.
- Derive Archimedes' Principle.
- Relate buoyancy to displaced volume.
- Explain neutral buoyancy.
- Connect Boyle's Law with Archimedes' Principle.

# 3.1 Hydrostatic Pressure

The pressure in a fluid at rest is

$$
P(h)=P_0+\rho gh
$$

where $P_0$ is atmospheric pressure.

# 3.2 Pressure Distribution

Pressure acts in every direction.

Because the lower surface of a submerged body is deeper than the upper surface, it experiences a greater pressure.

Horizontal forces cancel.

The remaining resultant acts upward.

> **Figure placeholder:** Pressure distribution on a submerged block.

# 3.3 Derivation of Archimedes' Principle

Let the body have cross-sectional area $A$ and height $\Delta h$.

The pressure difference is

$$
\Delta P=\rho g\Delta h.
$$

The upward force is

$$
F_B=\Delta P\,A.
$$

Since

$$
V=A\Delta h,
$$

we obtain

$$
\boxed{F_B=\rho gV}
$$

::: {.callout-important title="DiveLab Insight"}

Archimedes transforms **volume** into **force**.

:::

# 3.4 Weight, Buoyancy and Equilibrium

Weight is

$$
W=mg.
$$

The net force is

$$
F_{net}=F_B-W.
$$

Neutral buoyancy occurs when

$$
F_B=W.
$$

# 3.5 Applications to Scuba Diving

Increasing the gas volume inside the BCD increases displaced water and therefore buoyancy.

The same principle applies to lungs, dry suits and bubbles.

# 3.6 From Physics to Systems

```text
Depth
    ↓
Pressure
    ↓
Volume
    ↓
Buoyant Force
```

The next chapter will add Newton's Second Law to transform force into motion.

# Chapter Summary

- Pressure increases with depth.
- Pressure differences generate buoyancy.
- Archimedes' Principle follows from hydrostatics.
- Buoyant force is proportional to displaced volume.
- Boyle and Archimedes together link pressure to force.

# Key Equations

| Equation | Interpretation |
|:---------|:---------------|
| $P(h)=P_0+\rho gh$ | Hydrostatic pressure |
| $F_B=\rho gV$ | Archimedes' Principle |
| $W=mg$ | Weight |
| $F_{net}=F_B-W$ | Net force |

# Exercises

1. Derive Archimedes' Principle from the hydrostatic pressure field.
2. Explain why the horizontal pressure forces cancel.
3. Calculate the buoyant force for 10 L of displaced seawater.
4. Explain neutral buoyancy.
5. Draw the chain Depth → Pressure → Volume → Buoyant Force.

# Looking Ahead

Boyle transformed pressure into volume.

Archimedes transformed volume into force.

Newton will transform force into motion.
